name: Ablabius Illustrius
bio: Ablabius Illustrius is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors gives no firm date for the poet. Paton's index lists the poet among the writers of the Cycle of Agathias, the sixth-century anthology.
This archive carries the 1 epigram ascribed to the poet in the third volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Book IX: 762).

poems.title: Book IX, 762: On the Quoit of Asclepiades
poems.author: Ablabius Illustrius
poems.text: Hephaestus wrought me with long labour, but Cytherea took me secretly from her husband’s chamber and gave me to Anchises as a souvenir of their stolen intercourse. Asclepiades found me among the descendants of Aeneas.
